subject: english
question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.**

Critics and Monday morning quarterbacks are (**a dime a dozen**), but it remains to be seen.

options.text: Anything that is common and easy to get
Avoiding the main topic, not speaking directly about the issue
To force an issue that has already ended
Stuck between two very bad options

solution:
The correct answer is **"Anything that is common and easy to get."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The expression **"a dime a dozen"** is an idiomatic phrase used to convey that something is very common, abundant, or easily found. (कोई चीज़ बहुत सामान्य, प्रचुर या आसानी से पाई जाने वाली है)
 
• It implies that the item or person in question is not rare or valuable and is, instead, quite commonplace.
 
 
• **Example**: *Talented singers are **a dime a dozen**__ in this music competition.*
 
 
 
• The phrase suggests that the thing being referred to is so plentiful that it is not particularly special or noteworthy.
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.
